reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it presents effortless token creation as genuine mining and encourages viewers to reproduce the process by submitting tokens through the OneLife interface. The speaker claims that token balances are doubled and that 50,000 coins are created per minute, while also saying no resources or further action are required, framing a click-based token-crediting mechanism as mining income.

the 5500 remember this split is double 2 is 11,000 and in total touch they are 22,000 touch
the mining process is very very very fast since 50 thousand coins are created every minute
we have to spend resources no what to do anything more
we are going to create all the tokens that we have in the account

opening.argument: The recording should be read cautiously as a limited account walkthrough, not as a promise of financial returns. Its stated purpose is operational: the speaker says he will show viewers how to send tokens, and describes what the interface reports after submission. Those statements establish the narrator's account of an on-screen process, but they do not independently establish value, convertibility, or any guaranteed outcome. Even the rapid-creation statement is presented as a description of the platform's process, not a quantified investment return. A careful viewer would therefore distinguish reported interface activity from proof that an asset has economic value.

citations.quote: in this short video I'll show you how to send tokens in OneCoin
the tokens have been successfully minered
the mining process is very very very fast since 50 thousand coins are created every minute

rebuttal.rebuttal: The opposing account treats the title and the speaker's platform description as proof of deception. But a title saying how to mine tokens identifies the subject, while the cited doubling and speed statements describe what the interface or platform is said to do; neither quote proves a guaranteed monetary return. The statement about resources concerns the described procedure, not a promise that viewers will profit.

citations.quote: How to Mine OneCoin Tokens on the New OneLife Platform
we have to spend resources no what to do anything more

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The walkthrough does more than neutrally report an interface: it directs the viewer through submission and presents the resulting credit as mining. The speaker says the tokens are successfully mined and emphasizes creation of 50,000 coins per minute. Calling this a limited report does not explain why a click-based credit should be understood as genuine asset acquisition.

citations.quote: we are going to create all the tokens that we have in the account
the tokens have been successfully minered
50 thousand coins are created every minute

opening.argument: This is best characterized as an instructional technology demonstration. The speaker explicitly introduces it as a short video showing how to send tokens, then narrates account navigation, token selection, submission, and checking account statistics. The title likewise frames the subject as using a platform. That tutorial structure matters: demonstrating where controls are and what messages appear is different from certifying the platform's economics. The material's central activity is explaining an interface workflow, so the evidence supports an operational-education classification rather than an inference that the creator is soliciting deceptive investment.

citations.quote: How to Mine OneCoin Tokens on the New OneLife Platform

Right click on Submit

rebuttal.rebuttal: The opposing account calls the demonstration an encouragement to reproduce a scam, but it does not identify an investment pitch, personal solicitation, or request for payment in the quoted material. The narration is procedural: it explains clicking Submit and inspecting My Account. Describing a platform workflow, even one involving tokens, is not by itself proof that the tutorial's subject is fraudulent.

citations.quote: in this short video I'll show you how to send tokens in OneCoin
If we go to where it says my account to verify

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The instructional format does not neutralize the substance being taught. The tutorial directs viewers to submit tokens, says they are successfully mined, and concludes that mining requires only a couple of clicks. That is not merely a neutral interface tour; it presents the low-effort crediting mechanism as a way to obtain additional tokens.

citations.quote: Click on submit
as simple as that of mining touch any that is enough with a couple of click
we have to spend resources no what to do anything more

opening.argument: Even accepting the platform's own terminology, the record does not show the core mechanics of a conventional scam transaction. The described action is submitting tokens already displayed in an account, followed by checking token and account statistics. The supplied material does not show a deposit request, a promise of guaranteed return, a credential request, or downline-income instruction. Nor does it establish that the displayed balances can be exchanged for money. The evidence therefore supports, at most, a demonstration of an account service's token feature, without enough proof to classify the service itself as deceptive.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The opposing account infers a scam mechanism from token creation, but the quoted evidence does not show money being requested or a return being guaranteed. It describes account balances and a submission flow. A platform's unusual terminology or unsupported economic model may warrant skepticism, but skepticism is not proof that the demonstrated service is deceptive.

citations.quote: all the tokens that we have in the account

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The absence of a spoken deposit request does not make the mechanism ordinary. The video teaches viewers to submit existing tokens and calls the resulting credit mining, while claiming that tokens are doubled and created rapidly without resources. Those claims offer apparent asset acquisition through a minimal action, which is the relevant deceptive mechanism even without a separate cash solicitation.
